name: LAMB2-related Infantile-Onset Nephrotic Syndrome

criteria.description: Onset of nephrotic syndrome within the first year of life
Identification of pathogenic variants in the LAMB2 gene
Presence of congenital ocular abnormalities such as microcoria

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of infantile-onset nephrotic syndrome plus pathogenic LAMB2 gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Ocular abnormalities support diagnosis but are not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic small, fixed pupils unresponsive to light
Severe proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and edema presenting in infancy
Deficiency confirmed by immunohistochemistry or genetic testing
searchTerms: muscle and kidney problems from laminin beta-2 lack

common.notes: Low serum albumin levels secondary to proteinuria
Decline in kidney function over months to years

occasional.notes: Reduced muscle tone observed in some patients
Mild to moderate delay in motor and cognitive milestones

searchTerms: eye abnormalities other than small pupils
ocular defects excluding small pupil size

occasional.notes: Elevated blood pressure secondary to renal impairment
Rare gastrointestinal protein loss contributing to hypoalbuminemia

rare.notes: Occasional seizures reported in severe cases
Secondary to fluid overload in renal failure
Rare complications due to hypercoagulable state
Poor growth due to chronic illness

laboratory: Hypoalbuminemia and hyperlipidemia on serum chemistry
Elevated serum creatinine indicating renal impairment
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal to increased echogenicity
Ocular imaging demonstrating microcoria and other anterior segment abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic biallelic mutations in the LAMB2 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Renal biopsy showing diffuse mesangial sclerosis and absence or reduction of laminin beta-2 staining

distinguishingFeatures: Histology showing diffuse mesangial sclerosis without laminin beta-2 deficiency

redFlags: Onset of nephrotic syndrome within first year of life
Rapid progression to end-stage renal disease
references: Zenker M, et al. Human laminin beta2 deficiency causes congenital nephrosis with mesangial sclerosis and distinct eye abnormalities. Hum Mol Genet. 2004.
Sado Y, et al. Pierson syndrome: laminin beta2 deficiency causes congenital nephrotic syndrome and ocular defects. Kidney Int. 2005.
Orphanet Report Series: LAMB2-related infantile-onset nephrotic syndrome. Orphanet. 2023.
